145	### 2. Dirty-mark-then-draw
146	
147	**The handler contract.** The kernel invokes each subscriber handler through a registered `Callable` with a reused `NotifyContext` (ADR-0003 § 3), exactly like every other kernel-invoked callable. The shape is ADR-0003's, as fixed by ADR-0004 § 2 (re-read 2026-10-28; it matches):
148	
149	```gdscript
150	func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken:
151		_dirty.absorb(batch)        # ADR-0004 DirtyAccumulator (capacity facet.key_capacity); allocates nothing; is_all on overflow
152		return ctx.complete()       # last statement; nothing follows it
153	```
154	
155	This replaces the architecture document's `-> void` example (§ GDD sync). A handler **must** do only this: copy the batch's keys into the presenter's pre-sized dirty structure, copy the scalar fields it needs from an event record into a fixed-size ring, and return. A handler **must never**: read a view, touch a node, create a `Callable` or a container, emit an engine signal, `await` (ADR-0003's identity check turns a coroutine state into a recorded `INCOMPLETE`, which counts against the handler), call `submit`, or write any property. A handler fault is counted and never fatal (ADR-0003).
156	
157	**Why the handler does not draw.** It runs inside P5 with writes disabled and its cost is added to every other subscriber's; a catch-up frame already runs the tick loop up to four times (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`) and `INPUT_SURFACE` handlers run once per tick. Reading views there would also read a state that a later tick in the same frame is about to replace.
158	
159	**Delivery recap (properties this ADR relies on; ADR-0004 owns the mechanism):**
160	- PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches arrive **once per rendered frame**, after the frame's last tick, one `ChangeBatch` per dirty block per subscription, with the union of the frame's keys (`is_all` true past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; this text's "`ALL`" means `batch.is_all`). INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick's batch. A 0-tick frame delivers nothing.
161	- A restore delivers one `is_all` batch per block to every class when `LOADING` becomes `RUNNING`, with `batch.tick` set to the restored `T` (ADR-0004 P5/load delivery). **ADR-0004 carries no other restore marker**, so `is_all` is indistinguishable from a mass change (§ 6).
162	- Notifications carry no state; event records (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`) carry identifiers only.
163	
164	**The draw side.** Each presenter keeps two things, and its `present(frame)` early-outs only when both are empty:
165	- `dirty`: which blocks or keys changed since its last draw. Dirty drives **bulk and structural reads** (lists, queries, rebuilds, layout of plates): a presenter performs a bulk read of a block only when that block, or `ALL`, is dirty (TR-instr-005: derived inputs refresh once per Graph step because the Graph dirties its keys once per step, never per frame).
166	- `animating`: whether anything still moves on `tick_alpha` or `present_time` (an interpolated position, a needle ramp, a fade, flow scroll). **Interpolation needs a draw on frames with no notification**, because a 144 fps frame between two ticks has a new `tick_alpha` and no new state; the example in `architecture.md` that returns when `_dirty.is_empty()` would freeze motion on those frames and is corrected. Cheap scalar getters on the `interpolated` pair (previous and current position) may be read every frame while `animating`.
167	- `ALL` means "rebuild everything from the views, and draw the end state with no transition": the correct and sufficient response both to a restore and to a mass change. A presenter bounds a rebuild by its own budget (PROJECTOR: `BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME`, chunked across frames, continuing to draw the last complete state until the chunks finish).
168	- Event records are copied into a fixed ring; ring overflow degrades to a full rebuild and counts `PRESENTER_EVENT_OVERFLOW`. Events are never dropped silently, and a `BODY_TRANSFER` is delivered to the camera as a rebase, not a cut (TR-shipbody-049; the rebase math is ADR-0008's).
169	
170	**Coherence by construction.** The driver runs after the TickDriver in the same `_process` pass (priorities -50 then 0) and the kernel cannot tick while presentation runs, so every presenter in a frame reads the same committed tick `T`. No presenter copies state to be consistent.
171	
172	**Latency, stated honestly.** Discrete committed state (a bead appears, a light toggles) is drawn in the same rendered frame as the P5 that announced it, with zero frames of delay (TR-assembly-045). Continuously interpolated motion lags the commit by up to one tick by construction, because `tick_alpha` is clamped at 1 and never extrapolates (PR-4 rule 3, PR-9 rate table).
173	
174	**A debug-build safety net, in addition to ADR-0004's check that every changed block marked a dirty key:** every presenter exposes `rebuild_signature() -> int` in debug and test builds only (a hash of the presenter's derived draw model). The dirty-correctness test (Validation) runs a scripted command stream through an incrementally updated presenter and a fresh presenter fed `ALL`, and requires equal signatures. A presenter that forgot to react to a key is caught by that test, not in play.
175	
176	### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages
177	
178	**A single `PresentationHost` node** (`extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code) owns a `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls `driver.frame(...)` from its `_process`. The host is the Pipeline root or a node it owns (ADR-0008 decides which; either way exactly one node). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.
179	
180	This is the "explicit driver" the HUD GDD asks for (OQ-HS-44, OQ-HS-51, ADR candidate F). It replaces N nodes whose relative order would depend on priority sub-constants and tree order with one loop over a fixed-size array, which is testable headless with stub presenters (AC-HS-89) and does not depend on the cross-node `process_priority` result that KRN-LAT-02 has not yet confirmed for a rendering build. Only the order **host after TickDriver** depends on ADR-0001's verified order.
181	
182	```gdscript
183	# src/presentation/presentation_stage.gd. Named constants only; nobody writes a literal stage number.
184	class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted
185	const PROJECT: int = 0         # PROJECTOR builds and rebuilds, chunked
186	const CAMERA_SOLVE: int = 1    # CameraSolver computes pose_q and world_to_hud; the canvas write is in frame_pre_draw
187	const AVATAR: int = 2          # Avatar Presenter: position, frame, flip, beam pose
188	const FILTER: int = 3          # Perception Filter step, decoy list, perceived() memo
189	const INSTRUMENTS: int = 4
190	const HUD: int = 5
191	const LIGHTING: int = 6        # reads the beam pose (AVATAR) and the decoy list (FILTER)
192	const TRAIL: int = 7           # Failure & Trail (truth channel, reads no Filter product)
193	const AUDIO: int = 8
194	const DEBUG: int = 9
195	```
196	
197	**The pinned partial order and why this total order satisfies it.** Every source that states an edge is satisfied:
198	- HUD AC-HS-89 and TR-hud-022: camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting. Stages 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.
199	- PF-35 and TR-percfilter-025: Avatar, then Filter, then Lighting reads the decoy list. Stages 2, 3, 6.
200	- TR-pc-040: the Presenter's beam pose is written before Lighting applies. Stages 2, 6.
201	- Instruments call `perceived()`, so they follow the Filter. Stages 3, 4.
202	- The rest (Trail, Audio, Debug after Lighting) is a convention. It differs from the order in `architecture.md` § Data Flow (Avatar, Lighting, Trail, Instruments, HUD, Audio), which the three GDD-stated edges override; § GDD sync lists the rewrite.
203	- **Camera versus Avatar.** Pipeline C2 asks for the camera "ordered after the actor" so that both compose the same interpolated position. This ADR gets the same guarantee by construction, not by order: the solver and the Avatar Presenter both call `Placement.at` with the same `PresentFrame` values, so they cannot disagree. The solver runs first because the HUD needs `world_to_hud` before it draws (TR-hud-022). Step 12 of the pipeline spike (zero render-px disagreement) tests the claim.
204	
205	```gdscript
206	class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted
207	var name: StringName
208	var stage: int                        # a PresentationStage constant
209	var reads: Array[int]                 # stages whose products this presenter calls; each must be < stage
210	var present: Callable                 # (frame: PresentFrame) -> void
211	var on_discontinuity: Callable        # (kind: int) -> void; DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE or DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT
212	
213	class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted     # one object, reused every frame; fields overwritten, never reallocated
214	var alpha: float            # clock.tick_alpha read ONCE per frame; in [0, 1]; 1.0 while not RUNNING
215	var T: int                  # last committed tick; may feed values the simulation also computes, never cosmetic phase
216	var running: bool
217	var present_time: float     # supplied by the Pipeline root (ADR-0008); frozen while PAUSED; the only cosmetic clock
218	var render_delta: float     # for smoothing filters only; never a phase
219	
220	class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted
221	func register(desc: PresenterDescriptor) -> void          # BOOTING only
222	func freeze() -> void                                      # sorts by stage; checks reads < stage; unique names; fails boot otherwise
223	func frame(host_delta: float, present_time: float) -> void # fills PresentFrame, handles load_seq, runs the stages
224	func notify_camera_cut() -> void                           # called by the camera stage; next frame every presenter gets CAMERA_CUT
225	```
226	
227	`present` and `on_discontinuity` are registered `Callable`s returning `void`. They are **not** kernel-invoked owner callables, so ADR-0003's `CompletionToken` rule does not apply to them, and registering `Callable`s rather than overriding a base class avoids the 4.7 typed-return override rule altogether (ADR-0003 § 1 makes the same choice for owners). If ADR-0010 picks an `@abstract` base class instead, `-> void` overrides need no `return`.
228	
229	**Driver rules.** The driver iterates a fixed-size array, allocates nothing, checks `present.is_valid()` before each call and skips and counts a freed presenter (`PRESENTER_DEAD`, as ADR-0002 does for result handlers), and **never runs a presenter inside a tick**. Presenter faults cannot fault the kernel: nothing here runs in a tick phase. Stage timing exists in dev and playtest builds through ADR-0001's diagnostics timer and is compiled out of release.
230	
231	**The frame object is the clock.** `PresentFrame.alpha` is read once; no presenter reads `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` directly (a lint on `tick_alpha` outside the driver, the camera solver's pure-function twin and tests). This guarantees one alpha per frame. A presenter may read `frame.T` for values the simulation also computes (the beacon aim at `T`, a Graph step index); it **must never** use `T` or any tick counter as cosmetic phase (registry `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`), and uses `frame.present_time` for cosmetic phase.
232	
233	**Pause.** `PresentFrame.present_time` is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED` and `alpha` is 1.0, so a presenter that computes from `present_time` and `alpha` is frozen without being told. Layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table) keep running on engine time because they must respond while paused (PR-9); they are INPUT_SURFACE objects and UI Controls, not world presenters.
234	
235	### 4. Integer placement at `tick_alpha`
236	
237	One function, one owner, no other rounding anywhere in presentation.
238	
239	```gdscript
240	# src/presentation/placement.gd
241	class_name Placement extends RefCounted
242	## Interpolate previous to current at alpha, then floor, per axis. alpha is clamped by the caller's PresentFrame.
243	static func at(prev: Vector2i, curr: Vector2i, alpha: float) -> Vector2i:
244		return Vector2i(floori(prev.x + (curr.x - prev.x) * alpha), floori(prev.y + (curr.y - prev.y) * alpha))
245	
246	## Alpha for a block whose owner runs every n ticks and publishes the tick it last ran (Horror alpha_5, PR-9).
247	static func alpha_n(run_tick: int, T: int, alpha: float, n: int) -> float:
248		return clampf((float(T - run_tick) + alpha) / float(n), 0.0, 1.0)
249	
250	## The only assignment point for a Node2D position in presentation. Skips an unchanged write.
251	static func put(node: Node2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
252		var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)
253		if node.position != v:
254			node.position = v
255	```
256	
257	**Rules:**
258	- Every moving thing in the current body frame is placed with `Placement.at` and written with `Placement.put`: sprites, the avatar, hand tools, the beam chest point, light origins, HUD plate anchors that follow world things, the single floored canvas offset of a non-avatar body (`Placement.at(off_prev, off_curr, alpha)` with both offsets taken relative to the avatar's body, TR-shipbody-033), and the camera pose. The beam's chest point and the Avatar sprite use the same rounded position, so light origin and sprite never disagree (PR-4 rule 2, TR-pc-026).
259	- **`floori`, never `int()`, `round`, `roundi` or truncation.** Probed 2026-10-28: `floori(-3 + 1 * 0.5)` is -3. Truncation and rounding both move negative-coordinate bodies by a pixel relative to positive ones.
260	- **Interpolate, then quantise (PR-4 rule 3).** Snap is a floor, not a filter: a body moving one base pixel per tick shows a k by k block step at interpolated timing, never twice in a frame at 60 fps and above, never backward. Nothing is rounded before the lerp.
261	- `alpha` is `frame.alpha`, in [0, 1], never extrapolated. `alpha_n` is legal only for a block whose owner publishes its run tick, is clamped at 1, and is floored by `at`. The sprite pose of a stepped rig (Horror) is not tweened; only the record's position is placed with `alpha_n` (PR-9).
262	- **Assignments to `position`, `global_position`, `transform`, `global_transform`, `offset` or `canvas_transform` on a `Node2D` or `CanvasItem` appear only in `placement.gd`** (and in the camera host's one `canvas_transform` write); a lint enforces it. A debug-build and integration-test sweep reads every `Node2D` under the world root once per frame in the scripted walk and asserts a zero fractional part (`PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL` counts, test fails on non-zero).
263	- No per-node scale animation; horizontal flip is `flip_h` or a scale of -1 on x only; `Camera2D.zoom` stays (1, 1); rotation of human-built geometry is 0 (PR-4 rules 4 and 5). Cosmetic offsets (tremor of plus or minus 1 art px) are integers added after placement.
264	- `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` are on as a safety net, set to their required values in `project.godot` by the Pipeline's guard rails (PR-15; probed: both default `false`). **Nothing in this ADR relies on them**; what they snap to under the SubViewport variants is ADR-0008's spike.
265	- An asset or one-off sprite uses even cell dimensions or `centered = false` with an integer `offset` (PR-4 rule 6); the asset lint is ADR-0010's.
266	
267	### 5. One interpolator: physics interpolation off, and no engine clock on sim-visible content
268	
269	**The pins.** `physics/common/physics_interpolation = false` in `project.godot`, written explicitly by the Pipeline's guard-rail block (PR-15; a value equal to the default is not serialised, so the tests read the effective value). The presentation root nodes set `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF`; children inherit. `Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled = false` and `limit_smoothed = false` where a `Camera2D` exists at all (the primary camera variant has none in the world tree, PR-6 C2).
270	
271	**The boot check, after the first frame** (probed: inheritance resolves in a running tree and not before): `ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/common/physics_interpolation") == false`, `get_tree().physics_interpolation == false`, and a walk over every node under the presentation roots asserts `not node.is_physics_interpolated()`. A violation fails boot in dev and playtest builds and counts `PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_ON` plus logs in release. A gdUnit4 test additionally turns `SceneTree.physics_interpolation` on, builds the presentation tree, and asserts `is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()` is false for every node, which proves the `OFF` roots rather than only the project setting.
272	
273	**Why not use the engine's 2D interpolation.** (a) It would be a second interpolator on a second clock (PR-4 rule 8). (b) Probed: `get_global_transform_interpolated` does not exist on `Node2D`, so no script could read where an engine-interpolated body is actually drawn, and the camera, which follows the un-interpolated pose, would swim against the sprite by 1 to 3 render pixels at 144 fps while looking fine at 60. (c) The kernel's previous and current pair is the only definition of the previous pose that survives a restore, a body transfer and a snap (`snap_baseline`, ADR-0003).
274	
275	**Engine clocks on sim-visible content.** `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D.play()` and `GPUParticles2D` at a non-zero `speed_scale` run on the engine's process time, which does not stop under kernel `PAUSED` (the tree is not paused, ADR-0001 § 6) and does not follow reduced motion. For world content (layer 0) and the HUD (layer 2) a presenter therefore **drives animation from `frame.present_time`** (a frame index computed from it, a shader time parameter set from it) or sets `speed_scale` to 0 while `present_time` is frozen. Engine-clocked animation is permitted only on layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table and menus), which must respond under pause, and on content that has no sim-visible meaning and is allowed to continue. Whether `speed_scale = 0` freezes a given node type exactly is UNVERIFIED (PRES-SPIKE-1).
276	
277	The bounded presentation-owned animation states are those PR-8 admits (camera state, and the instruments' `settle_response`), plus the cosmetic scalars of § 6.
278	
279	### 6. Presentation-local state, the restore edge, and pure-function presenters
280	
281	**What presentation may keep.** A presenter may hold a scalar or small structure (a needle's settle triple, a dwell counter, a tremor envelope, a fade, a cull history, the camera's smoothing state, a numeral throttle) **if and only if**:
282	1. it is never persisted, hashed, replicated or read by the simulation (`src/kernel/` and `src/sim/` import nothing from `src/presentation/`);
283	2. it changes how a value *arrives* and never what it *settles to*, and never decides visibility of a truth-channel element (a trail's visibility depends only on the sim, which is why the Failure & Trail GDD calls it a pure reader);
284	3. it is reset by `on_discontinuity` on a restore, a new game, a camera cut and `hard_start` (TR-instr-002, TR-attention-047);
285	4. the presenter's registration lists it in a short doc comment so a reviewer can see the scalars (the lint cannot).
286	
287	**A presenter's drawn output is a pure function** of `(PresentationViews at this frame, PresentFrame, its resettable scalars)`. The first frame after a restore needs no special path: `ALL` rebuilds from views, `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)` clears the scalars, and the kernel's `snap_baseline` has made previous equal current, so there is no interpolation across the break (TR-cmd-046, TR-horror-041, TR-attention-047, TR-webmap-039 restore half). A multi-beat stall plays at most one beat and never replays (TR-attention-047): a presenter keeps the last-seen sequence value it was shown, compares it with the view's, and on a jump of more than one shows the end state.
288	
289	**Edge detection by sequence counters.** A presenter detects a discrete source change by comparing a view's sequence counter to the value it last saw (`breath_src_change_seq`, TR-suit-041), not by counting notifications, because merged delivery turns N ticks into one batch. Because the notification, the dirty mark and the draw happen in one rendered frame, a click can start in the Audio stage and the dial swap land in the Instruments stage of the same frame.
290	
291	**The restore edge is not `ALL`.** `ALL` also means "more than 256 keys changed this frame" (a weld can do it), and resetting an instrument's tremor on a weld is wrong. The driver therefore watches a dedicated counter:
292	
293	```gdscript
294	# Requested of ADR-0001's PresentationClock (read-only, not a state block, never hashed or saved):
295	var load_seq: int:      # +1 on every transition into RUNNING that follows LOADING, and on every new game
296		get: return _driver_load_seq
297	```
298	
299	At the top of `frame(...)` the driver compares `clock.load_seq` with the last seen value and, on a change, calls every presenter's `on_discontinuity(DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE)` **before** any `present`. Camera cuts arrive the other way: the camera stage calls `driver.notify_camera_cut()` and the next frame delivers `DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT` (reset of instrument scalars and cull history; Instruments IW-33). `BODY_TRANSFER` is a rebase, not a cut, unless the new body's limits clamp (TR-shipbody-049, ADR-0008). If ADR-0001's owner declines the extra field, the equivalent is a composition-root-owned counter on the same clock object (ADR-0004's draft has no restore marker in `ChangeBatch`; its `is_all` on load is the same value as a mass change); the driver is the only consumer either way, so the choice does not leak into presenters.
300	
301	### 7. `INPUT_SURFACE` is the only submitting class, and a class is not a right
302	
303	- A command can be submitted only by an object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002) **and** was registered as `INPUT_SURFACE`. Subscribing as `INPUT_SURFACE` confers no submit right (registry `presentation_submit_without_handle`): the Interaction prompt object subscribes without a handle. A `PRESENTATION` facet has no submit method and no way to obtain a handle.
304	- **Boot check at the freeze:** every handle name in the kernel's issued-handle table corresponds to a subscription registered as `INPUT_SURFACE` with the same name; a handle issued to a name with no `INPUT_SURFACE` registration, or to a `PRESENTATION` subscriber, fails boot. This ties ADR-0002's table to this ADR's class (ADR-0004's `subscribe` carries the diagnostic name as its `name` argument).
305	- **Where a submit call may occur.** An `INPUT_SURFACE` object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` submits from **its own `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`**, exactly as the Input Adapter does (ADR-0001 § 2 already lets any registered INPUT_SURFACE node run below `TICK_DRIVER`, and § 3 puts the Adapter there). A UI surface (Chart Table menus later, the Interaction prompt if it ever submits) **latches an intent in a plain field in its UI callback** and submits it from that `_process`, so its commands are queued before the driver's tick loop and reach the same tick as the Adapter's. It **never** calls `submit` from an engine signal handler, `_gui_input`, `_input`, `_physics_process`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object (ADR-0001 guideline restated). The control plane is different: `ControlHandle` calls are recorded when made, from any phase (CR-15), so a UI button calling `PauseGate` from its signal handler is legal. This ADR therefore adds no second submit location and no driver stage for submission.
306	- **Result handlers.** The kernel flushes the result buffer in the driver, before presentation; an `INPUT_SURFACE` result handler is a kernel-invoked callable and obeys the same contract as a subscriber handler: it records the result into a fixed ring and returns `ctx.complete()`. Display of a rejection happens in the object's own presenter step (the stage it is registered for), never in the handler.
307	- **The rule is per object, not per system** (CR-10): a HUD that grows a button splits into the HUD presenter (`PRESENTATION`) and a small `INPUT_SURFACE` intent object.
308	- Presentation predicts no outcome; the Adapter's pre-play of body motion and sound keyed by `correlation` is ADR-0019's, and light and effects change only on committed state (kernel anti-target: no client-side prediction at MVP).
309	
310	### 8. Engine signals stay inside presentation
311	
312	Engine signals (`signal`, `.connect(...)`) are used **between presentation objects for user-initiated events only** (a card opens, a setting changes, a button is pressed). They are never the kernel's notification transport (ADR-0004 § 1 decides a kernel-owned observer registry of Callables and no engine signals; this ADR agrees), never carry simulation values into a simulation module, and are never declared or connected in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/` (a lint; the simulation is scene-tree free). A signal is not a way around the stage-read rule: a presenter that needs another presenter's per-frame product reads it through a declared `reads` edge, not through a connection.
313	
314	### Key Interfaces
315	
316	```gdscript
317	# ----- Issued by the composition root (ADR-0001 § 5); presentation objects receive only these -----
318	class_name PresentationFacet extends RefCounted        # see § 1
319	class_name PresentationClock extends RefCounted        # ADR-0001: tick_alpha, T, running (+ load_seq, requested)
320	
321	# ----- Handler (kernel-invoked; ADR-0003 callable contract; shape fixed by ADR-0004 § 2) -----
322	func _on_changes(batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken
323	
324	# ----- Driver (src/presentation/) -----
325	class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted        # constants, § 3
326	class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted      # § 3
327	class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted             # § 3
328	class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted       # register / freeze / frame / notify_camera_cut
329	class_name PresentationHost extends Node               # setup(driver); _process(delta) -> driver.frame(delta, present_time)
330	
331	# ----- Placement (src/presentation/placement.gd) -----
332	class_name Placement extends RefCounted                # at / alpha_n / put, § 4
333	
334	const DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE: int = 0
335	const DISCONTINUITY_CAMERA_CUT: int = 1
336	```
337	
338	### Implementation Guidelines
339	- **Must** subscribe through a `PresentationFacet` the composition root issued; **must never** hold the kernel, `SimViews`, a `WriteScope` or a tick-phase `ctx` in `src/presentation/`.
340	- **Must** write a subscriber handler as "mark dirty, copy event scalars, `return ctx.complete()`"; **must never** read a view, touch a node, allocate, emit a signal, `await` or submit in a handler.
341	- **Must** keep `dirty` and `animating` separate; **must never** return early on an empty dirty set while a value is animating.
342	- **Must** perform bulk or structural reads only when the block (or `ALL`) is dirty; scalar getters on the interpolated pair may be read each frame while animating.
343	- **Must** register one `PresenterDescriptor` per system with a stage from `PresentationStage` and a truthful `reads` list; **must never** write a literal stage number, define `_process` in a registered presenter, or read a product of the same or a later stage. The `_process` rule applies to objects registered through a `PresenterDescriptor`; the exemptions are `PresentationHost` (and the Pipeline root that may host it), `INPUT_SURFACE` objects at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`, and layer 3 and 4 UI Controls (PR-9).
344	- **Must** place every moving thing with `Placement.at` and `Placement.put`; **must never** use `int()`, `round`, `roundi`, a tween, an engine interpolation or any other rounding for a sim-owned position, and **must never** assign `position`, `global_position`, `transform` or `offset` outside `placement.gd`.
345	- **Must** read alpha only from `PresentFrame`; **must never** read `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` in a presenter, extrapolate past 1, or use `T` or a tick counter as cosmetic phase.
346	- **Must** animate sim-visible world and HUD content from `frame.present_time`; **must never** leave a free-running `Tween`, `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D` or particle clock on layer 0 or layer 2 content.
347	- **Must** keep `physics/common/physics_interpolation` false, put `physics_interpolation_mode = OFF` on the presentation roots, and pass the post-first-frame boot walk; **must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/presentation/` (ADR-0001).
348	- **Must** write only the allow-list of § 1; **must never** write `Camera2D.*`, `Viewport.*`, `SubViewport.*`, `SubViewportContainer.*` or `CanvasLayer.*` outside the Pipeline root and the camera host, and **must never** write a block, a command, a physics body, `SceneTree.paused`, `Engine.time_scale` or synthetic input.
349	- **Must** reset every presentation scalar in `on_discontinuity`; **must never** persist, hash, replicate or feed back a presentation scalar, or let one decide a truth-channel element's visibility.
350	- **Must** submit only from an object that is both an `INPUT_SURFACE` registration and a `SurfaceHandle` holder; **must never** call `submit` from a signal handler, `_gui_input`, a notification handler or a `PRESENTATION` object, and **must never** infer submit rights from the subscriber class.
351	- **Must** use signals only between presentation objects for user-initiated events; **must never** declare or connect an engine signal in `src/kernel/` or `src/sim/`.
352	- **Should** drive the driver with an injected `PresentFrame` in tests (stub presenters, injected `present_time`, no scene); **should** record stage timing only in dev and playtest builds.
353	
354	## Alternatives Considered

354	## Alternatives Considered
355	
356	### Alternative 1: Each presenter runs in its own `_process` at a named sub-priority of `PRESENTATION`
357	- **Description**: Add constants (`PRESENTATION + n`) per presenter in a presentation-owned file; every presenter node reads the clock itself. This is the shape `architecture.md`'s example implies and it keeps ADR-0001's "presentation nodes at `PRESENTATION` or greater" rule literally.
358	- **Pros**: Idiomatic Godot; no new host node; each presenter is an ordinary node with its own `_process`; no driver to maintain.
359	- **Cons**: Presenter order is N-way cross-node `process_priority` order, which KRN-LAT-02 has verified only headless for the three-constant case and not on a release export; each presenter reads the clock separately (nothing guarantees they see one alpha); order is untestable without a scene; a forgotten priority silently lands at 0 and runs in tree order; the HUD GDD explicitly asks for an explicit driver.
360	- **Rejection Reason**: The order is the contract (six TR rows), and an explicit array makes it testable and independent of an unverified engine behaviour. The cost is one small driver class. The decision is reversible: the `PresentationStage` constants map directly onto `PRESENTATION + n` priorities if the driver is ever dropped.
361	
362	### Alternative 2: Draw in a `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` handler on the Pipeline root (PR-8 item 3 as written)
363	- **Description**: One engine signal handler on the Pipeline root reads views and draws for every presenter just before the frame is drawn.
364	- **Pros**: Guarantees every presenter has run before the draw; one hook for the camera write and the presenters.
365	- **Cons**: `frame_pre_draw` never fired in the headless probe and its ordering against `_process` is UNVERIFIED (pipeline spike steps 11 and 12), so every presenter would inherit an unverified dependency; presenters would run in an engine signal callback that the headless unit tests cannot trigger; the kernel's tick order guarantee (driver before presentation) is stated for `_process`, not for this signal.
366	- **Rejection Reason**: The only work that must happen in the draw phase is the `canvas_transform` write, and it stays there (ADR-0008). Presenters run in `_process`, where the order is stated, testable and already the foundation of ADR-0001.
367	
368	### Alternative 3: Handlers read views and update nodes directly (draw in the handler)
369	- **Description**: The P5 handler does the reading and the node writes.
370	- **Pros**: Least code; no dirty bookkeeping; the draw happens as soon as state is committed.
371	- **Cons**: Writes happen inside P5, where a long handler stalls every other subscriber; in a catch-up frame it would redraw for intermediate ticks nobody will see (PRESENTATION delivery is already merged for exactly this reason); it cannot interpolate on frames that have no tick; it would read views that the kernel's own contract says are only coherent after P4.
372	- **Rejection Reason**: Contradicts CR-10 and PR-8 item 3, and cannot serve a 144 fps render over a 60 Hz tick.
373	
374	### Alternative 4: Rely on the engine's snap flags (and `physics_interpolation`) instead of an explicit placement function
375	- **Description**: Leave positions as floats, turn on `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and the engine's 2D interpolation, and let the engine quantise.
376	- **Pros**: Almost no presentation code.
377	- **Cons**: Snapping happens on the engine's float transform after interpolation by the engine's clock (a second interpolator); the Pipeline GDD records that what the snap flags snap to under the SubViewport variants is not sourceable; rotated or parented nodes snap differently; the camera and the beam chest point would disagree with the sprite by a pixel; the result differs between 60 and 144 fps in ways no test can see.
378	- **Rejection Reason**: PR-4 rule 2 already calls the snap flags a safety net, not the mechanism. One pure function is the only form of this rule that a unit test can pin.
379	
380	### Alternative 5: Presenters keep their own previous and current caches and interpolate locally
381	- **Description**: Each presenter remembers last frame's value and lerps toward the new one.
382	- **Pros**: No dependence on `interpolated` blocks exposing a pair.
383	- **Cons**: Two definitions of "previous" (the presenter's and the kernel's); breaks at a restore, a body transfer or a hitch; moves the one interpolator into N places (PR-4 rule 8); a presentation that owns visibility-deciding state is no longer a truth channel (PR-8 rationale).
384	- **Rejection Reason**: The kernel's previous and current pair with `snap_baseline` is the only definition that survives discontinuities.
385	
386	### Alternative 6: Let `PRESENTATION` subscribers submit through a shared handle
387	- **Description**: Give the HUD and Chart Table a shared `SurfaceHandle` so UI can submit directly from its signal handlers.
388	- **Pros**: Simple for menus and prompts.
389	- **Cons**: Collapses the distinction ADR-0002 builds (a class is not a right); makes "presentation never writes the simulation" unenforceable; blocks co-op ingress from being added without changing owners.
390	- **Rejection Reason**: Contradicts the registered `presentation_submit_without_handle` pattern and kernel H4.
391	
392	## Consequences
393	
394	### Positive
395	- One place, one loop and one frame object decide presenter order and the alpha every presenter sees; the order is a list a headless test can assert, which closes the HUD GDD's ADR candidate F and settles the three-way disagreement over order.
396	- A handler has a single permitted shape (mark, copy, `return ctx.complete()`), so P5 cost is bounded by batch size and cannot draw or fault the kernel.
397	- Interpolation is one pure function; the camera, the beam, the sprite and a docked body's canvas offset agree by construction, and a cadence test needs no renderer.
398	- A restore needs no special presenter path: `ALL` plus a reset hook plus the kernel's `snap_baseline`.
399	- "Which class may submit" is now two checks (facet and handle) rather than a convention, and boot fails if the handle table and the class registrations disagree.
400	- The Layout PROJECTOR class rules and the write allow-list are stated once, in a form a lint can check.
401	
402	### Negative
403	- A new class (`PresentationDriver`), a registration step and a frozen registry for presenters. Dynamic presenters (one per instrument) are not registered individually: one registration per system iterates its own children.
404	- Presenters cannot use `_process`, so ordinary Godot idioms for animation (tweens, `AnimationPlayer`) are restricted on layer 0 and the HUD, which costs authoring convenience.
405	- One request lands on a neighbouring ADR (`PresentationClock.load_seq` on ADR-0001; ADR-0004's draft needs no change for the handler signature and has no restore marker, so the request has no fallback there), and several lint rules depend on ADR-0010's tool.
406	- The stage order beyond the three GDD-stated edges is a convention, and a GDD or `architecture.md` that disagrees must be edited (§ GDD sync).
407	
408	## Risks
409	- **R1: `frame_pre_draw` ordering fails the pipeline spike** (fires before `_process`, or not in a way the host can use). Mitigation: only the `canvas_transform` write depends on it, and PR-6 C2 already names the fallback (the Pipeline root's own `_process` at the lowest priority, which still precedes the draw). No presenter depends on it.
410	- **R2: Release-export `_process` order differs from the headless probe** (host not after the TickDriver). Mitigation: KRN-LAT-02 is a precondition of Accepting ADR-0001 and therefore of this ADR; the fallback is the sequential-parent design recorded in ADR-0001.
411	- **R3: `Placement.put`'s equality skip is wrong for a node whose transform is also set elsewhere.** Mitigation: the lint makes `placement.gd` the only assignment point, and the post-frame fractional sweep in tests catches a stray writer.
412	- **R4: A presenter forgets to react to a key** (the dirty set is correct but the presenter ignores it). Mitigation: the dirty-correctness equivalence test (`rebuild_signature`) and ADR-0004's debug check; the first catches presenter bugs, the second kernel-side marking bugs.
413	- **R5: 4.7 `CanvasItem` lines lose their antialiasing feather**, which makes any `draw_line` hairline thinner than the art assumed. Mitigation: out of this ADR's decision, but the write allow-list does not make `draw_*` a placement mechanism; instruments use pre-rendered needle frames (TR-instr-010); ADR-0028 and ADR-0030 own the line-drawing consequence.
414	- **R6: A freed presenter or a stale `Callable`** at teardown or scene change. Mitigation: `is_valid()` per call with `PRESENTER_DEAD`; the teardown test checks `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` returns to its pre-boot value, as ADR-0003 requires of owners.
415	- **R7: `speed_scale = 0` does not freeze a given particle or animation node.** Mitigation: UNVERIFIED and spike-bound (PRES-SPIKE-1); the fallback is to compute the frame index from `present_time` and not use the engine clock at all for that node.
416	- **R8: The stage list is wrong for a presenter nobody has designed yet** (Interaction prompt art, a future overlay). Mitigation: the stage list is a constants file; adding a stage renumbers nothing that anyone writes by hand (nobody writes a literal) and the `reads` check re-validates the graph at boot.
417	- **R9: The `load_seq` request is declined by ADR-0001's owner.** Mitigation: ADR-0004's draft has no restore marker, so the fallback is a counter bumped by the composition root's load host when `request_restore` or `request_new_game` completes (LOADING to RUNNING), exposed on the same `PresentationClock` object; only the driver consumes it either way. Either route must exist before Acceptance.
418

479	## Performance Implications
480	- **CPU**: The driver is a loop over at most 10 registered presenters with a validity check and a `Callable.call` each; it allocates nothing (one reused `PresentFrame`, one pre-sorted array). Handler cost is O(batch) merge into a pre-sized structure; it never reads a view. `Placement.put` skips an unchanged write. This ADR claims **no new millisecond budget**: presenter costs are already budgeted in their own GDDs and sum in ADR-0008's single draw-call and frame-time table (pipeline `_process` at most 0.5 ms, light CPU at most 1.0 ms steady, total frame at most 14.9 ms desktop and 30.0 ms Deck, P99, release export). Driver overhead is measured in PRES-SPIKE-1 and reported against the pipeline row, not given a number here.
481	- **Memory**: A fixed number of small objects at boot (driver, host, frame, one descriptor per presenter, one dirty structure per presenter). No per-frame allocation; verified by a flat `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` over N frames plus `is_same` identity of the `PresentFrame` and the descriptor array (OBJECT_COUNT counts only Objects, not arrays, per ADR-0007's note).
482	- **Load Time**: Presenter registration and the freeze happen in `BOOTING` with the kernel's registries; negligible.
483	- **Network**: None. Presentation is local; co-op peers draw their own views (kernel CR-10 notifications are identical for HOST and MIRROR).

499	## Validation Criteria
500	- **Order test (AC-HS-89):** a driver built with stub presenters in every stage, a stub Filter whose slew advances in its step, and an injected `PresentFrame` runs the stages in the `PresentationStage` order; the HUD reads the post-step value. A registry with a `reads` edge that is not strictly earlier fails `freeze()`.
501	- **Dirty-correctness equivalence:** per presenter, a scripted command stream through an incrementally updated presenter and a fresh presenter fed `ALL` yield equal `rebuild_signature()`.
502	- **Restore equivalence:** save at tick T, restore into a fresh presenter set, and compare the drawn signature with the continuing run after `on_discontinuity(RESTORE)`; both are the end state with scalars reset (TR-attention-047, TR-horror-041).
503	- **Placement:** property test over positive and negative prev and curr and alpha in [0, 1]: result is between `floor(prev)` and `curr`, never moves backward as alpha rises, equals `curr` at alpha 1.0, and `Placement.at` agrees across the camera and Avatar call sites for the same `PresentFrame`. A scripted walk with a fractional-position sweep every frame reports zero `PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL`. A 144, 120, 60 and 40 fps injected-delta fixture checks "never twice in a frame at 60 fps and above" and "alternating +1 and +2 at 40 fps" (PR-4 rule 3).
504	- **Cadence (TR-pc-039 half):** one command stream at 30, 60, 120 and 144 fps of injected delta: simulation blocks and per-tick presenter samples are byte-identical; per-frame placements are not claimed identical.
505	- **No physics interpolation:** the boot walk after the first frame passes; a test sets `SceneTree.physics_interpolation = true` and asserts `is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()` is false for every node under the presentation roots.
506	- **Zero allocation:** `Performance.OBJECT_COUNT` flat over 10,000 injected frames with the full stub stage set, and `PresentFrame` / descriptor array identity (`is_same`) unchanged.
507	- **Handler contract:** a handler fixture that reads a view, touches a node or allocates fails a counting stub (`HANDLER_VIEW_READ`, `HANDLER_NODE_WRITE` in test builds); every handler's last statement is `return ctx.complete()` (CI check shared with ADR-0003).
508	- **Class and handle:** a boot with a handle name that has no `INPUT_SURFACE` registration, or one issued to a `PRESENTATION` subscriber, fails; the Interaction prompt object subscribed as `INPUT_SURFACE` without a handle cannot submit.
509	- **Toggle isolation (TR-pxl-034):** the same command stream with each accessibility toggle on and off yields equal tick count and `state_hash`.
510	- **Lints (ADR-0010 decides the tool; each is regex, AST or a boot walk):** writes outside the allow-list; `_physics_process` anywhere in `src/presentation/`, and `_process` in an object registered through a `PresenterDescriptor` (exempt: `PresentationHost` or the Pipeline root, `INPUT_SURFACE` objects at `INPUT_ADAPTER`, layer 3 and 4 UI Controls); `tick_alpha` outside the driver; `position`/`transform` assignments outside `placement.gd`; `int(`, `round(` on a placement path; `signal` or `.connect(` in `src/kernel/` and `src/sim/`; `submit(` outside `INPUT_SURFACE` files; `Camera2D`/`Viewport` members outside the Pipeline root and camera host; `SimViews`/`WriteScope` in `src/presentation/`.
511	- **PRES-SPIKE-1 (release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, shared with KRN-LAT-02 and pipeline spike steps 11 and 12):** host `_process` runs after the TickDriver; `frame_pre_draw` fires after the host's `_process`; `speed_scale = 0` freezes `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimatedSprite2D` and `GPUParticles2D` under kernel `PAUSED`; driver overhead with ten stub presenters is reported against the pipeline row.

208:**6.1 The camera is a pure solver behind a host (TR-pxl-010, 011, 012, 013, 015; the formulas D.6 to D.10 are the GDD's).** `CameraSolver` is a `RefCounted` with `solve(input: SolverInput, state: SolverState, params: SolverParams) -> Pose`, no scene-tree dependency, float64 per-axis state held as scalars (not `Vector2`), `dt` clamped to `DT_MAX` (0.05 s). The **type of `SolverInput` is the enforcement of Camera C1**: it carries only the follow target's previous and current body-local positions, `tick_alpha`, the raw local beam aim, the zoom step, `dt`, and cut / rebase flags; it has no field through which Attention, breach, horrors, sound, the graph or sanity could enter, so the same input trace gives the same camera trace in calm, tell and breach by construction. The Perception Filter has no write path to a camera or viewport property (§ 2.6). Solver parameters and `ZOOM_MIN_K` are tuning tables loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline and injected. Camera state is never persisted: the host resets (`CUT`) the solver on every `LOADING → RUNNING` and every pod or transit body transfer, starting with `L = 0` easing in; a weld or detach `BODY_TRANSFER` carrying `frame_delta_px` calls `rebase(frame_delta_px)`, which shifts the follow and history and keeps lag and `L`. Owners of moving read views set `previous := current` in `post_restore` (ADR-0016), so the first frame after a restore interpolates nothing.
211:- **What is UNVERIFIED:** that `frame_pre_draw` fires after every `_process` of the frame and before the frame's draw, and that a `canvas_transform` written there is the one drawn (probed: the signal exists and does not fire headless). **Fallback and trigger:** if step 11/12 shows any `_process` running after the handler, or a one-frame disagreement between camera and sprite, the host's write moves to the `_process` of `PipelineRoot` at a priority later than every presentation node. ADR-0001's three constants have no such value, so this requires **adding `PRESENTATION_LATE` to `ProcessPriority` (an additive amendment to ADR-0001, requested in Open Question OQ-D)**; until then a literal priority is forbidden and the fallback is not built.

Also, `is_physics_interpolated()` **ignores the global enable flag** (a default node reads `true` even with `SceneTree.physics_interpolation` false; `is_physics_interpolated_and_enabled()` reads `false`), so the boot walk asserts explicit `Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF` inheritance, not effective interpolation. (3) **Probed (headless, and consistent in the windowed run):** with `process_priority` -50, 0, 0 and 5 on four sibling nodes, `_process` ran -50, then the two 0s in tree order, then 5, on all three frames; ties at one priority run in tree order, which is why this ADR hosts all presentation work in one node (§ 3). The release-export result belongs to KRN-LAT-02 (ADR-0001). (4) **Probed in a windowed Vulkan run of the 4.7.2 mono editor (2026-10-28):** per frame, `SceneTree` `_process`, then node `_process` in priority order (-50, 0, 5), then `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw`, then `frame_post_draw`. `frame_pre_draw` "never fired" in the headless run only because of the dummy renderer. This confirms that a `canvas_transform` write in `frame_pre_draw` lands after every presenter, and that a camera solve placed inside it would be invisible to the HUD stage (ADR-0008 adopts the solve in stage 1, § 3). `thread_model` read 1 (Single-Safe). **UNVERIFIED:** a release export, the D3D12 default on Windows, the Steam Deck, and `rendering/driver/threads/thread_model` = 2 (the thread that emits `frame_pre_draw` is not documented in the pinned reference); ADR-0008 pins `thread_model` at its default 1 and treats 2 as unsupported (TD-20); ADR-0008 pipeline spike steps 11 and 12 settle the rest. (5) **UNVERIFIED:** whether assigning an unchanged `Node2D.position` costs anything; `Placement.put` skips an equal write by design, so the ADR does not depend on the answer. (6) **Probed headless on 4.7.2:** `AnimationPlayer.speed_scale = 0` does not advance; `Tween.set_speed_scale(0)` does not advance; `AnimationPlayer.callback_mode_process = ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_MANUAL` with `advance(dt)` works exactly. **Inconclusive or untested:** `AnimatedSprite2D.speed_scale = 0` (inconclusive) and `GPUParticles2D.speed_scale = 0` (the dummy renderer does not simulate particles; the class docs say 0 pauses, not run). The primary pattern (§ 5) therefore needs none of the unverified cases; the particle case is a story-level check (§ Validation). (7) **Snap flags:** what `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` snap to is ADR-0008's (they snap in base-pixel space under pass B, and `canvas_transform` is in base-pixel units, probe E8 there); nothing here relies on them. |

### 1. Subscriber classes and what each may read and write

The class is chosen by the composition root at facet-issue time, not by the presenter. A presenter cannot subscribe as a class its facet was not issued for.

```gdscript
# src/kernel/facets/presentation_facet.gd (placement requested of ADR-0010, see "Facet-side types" in Key Interfaces).
# Issued by the composition root in BOOTING, one per presentation object, never the whole Kernel (ADR-0001 § 5).
# This is the class-bound wrapper around NotifyFacet: the composition root binds the SubscriberClass at issue (ADR-0004 § 2).
class_name PresentationFacet extends RefCounted
var views: PresentationViews          # ADR-0003 § 7; getter-only facades; the face (default or perception) follows perception_access
var clock: PresentationClock          # ADR-0001; read-only: tick_alpha, T, running, state, load_seq (§ 6)
var key_capacity: int                 # ADR-0004 NotifyFacet.key_capacity; sizes each presenter's DirtyAccumulator
var perception_access: bool           # read-only; set by the composition root at issue; true only on the Filter's facet and DIAGNOSTIC facets
## Subscription is per block (ADR-0004 § 2); a presenter that needs two blocks subscribes twice with the same method Callable.
## The class is fixed at issue; this forwards to NotifyFacet.subscribe(cls, block_id, handler, name). The handler must be a method Callable
## taking two arguments (ADR-0004 subscribe-time check 1: lambdas and .bind() results are refused). A subscription to a PERCEPTION_OUT block
## on a facet with perception_access == false is refused with SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED (ADR-0004 subscribe-time check 6) and returns an inactive handle.
func subscribe(block_id: StringName, handler: Callable, subscriber_name: StringName) -> SubscriptionHandle
# Content catalogs (ADR-0007) arrive as their own setup() arguments; they are frozen and read-only.
```

| Class | Facet is issued to | Reads | Writes | Submit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PRESENTATION` | Camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Lighting, Failure & Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, the Filter's host object | `PresentationViews` of SIM blocks (previous and current pairs), `PresentationClock`, the frame's `PresentFrame`, frozen content catalogs, **products of strictly earlier stages** (§ 3), the Filter's `perceived()` for corruptible values | Only the allow-list below | Never. The facet has no submit method. |
| `INPUT_SURFACE` | Input Adapter (holds the one `SurfaceHandle` at MVP), the Interaction prompt object (no handle), Chart Table menu objects (no handle at MVP) | As `PRESENTATION` | As `PRESENTATION` | **May be issued a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002); the class alone confers nothing.** Receives every tick's batch. A facet issued as `INPUT_SURFACE` is itself a registration whether or not it ever subscribes (§ 7). |
| `PROJECTOR` | Layout projector, `body.projector`, Lighting's occluder builder | As `PRESENTATION` | Engine-side *derived* objects its block owner's GDD names (nodes it creates, frees or reparents; tile and occluder content); declares the engine classes it may instantiate at registration | Never |
| `DIAGNOSTIC` | Debug Overlay (dev and playtest builds only; ADR-0031) | Everything, including kernel internals and `PERCEPTION_OUT`, through a separate diagnostics facet (`perception_access` true) | Its own overlay nodes only | Never |
| `REPLICATION` | Nobody at MVP (dormant until VS-B; ADR-0032) | n/a | n/a | n/a |

The scene shape that `body.projector` builds (per-body root, reparenting, Y-sort) is ADR-0034's; this ADR fixes only its class rights and its place in stage 0.

**Read rules, each lint- or boot-checked:**
- Presentation reads simulation state only through `PresentationViews` and `PresentationClock`. It never holds `Kernel`, `SimViews`, `WriteScope`, `Command`, `BlockDescriptor` or a tick-phase context (`CallContext`, `ValidateContext`, `ApplyContext`, `HookContext`, `SnapshotContext`). A lint forbids exactly those names in `src/presentation/` (ADR-0003 Risks already commits to it; the list is ADR-0010 ARCH-08's explicit deny list per TD-01). A handler legitimately names `ChangeBatch`, `NotifyContext` and `CompletionToken`, which are facet-side types (Key Interfaces).
- **`PERCEPTION_OUT` blocks are not subscribable or readable through a default `PresentationFacet`.** `perception_access` is `true` **only on the Perception Filter's facet and on `DIAGNOSTIC` facets, and `false` on every other facet** (the composition root sets it at issue; this ADR only declares which facets carry it). Enforcement is not ADR-0009's: (a) **subscribe time**, ADR-0004 subscribe-time check 6 (TD-08) refuses a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block from a facet without access with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED`, which closes ADR-0004 OQ-7; (b) **read time**, ADR-0003 § 7 (amended by TD-07 item 10) gives `PresentationViews` two faces selected by the same flag: the default face returns the block's `empty_view` and counts `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED`, the perception face returns the real facade. Lighting reads the Filter's per-viewer decoy list, an object the Filter owns, not the block. This follows `architecture.md` § API Boundaries ("Filter and Debug only") and Principle 3 over the broader wording in the kernel GDD's CR-10 table. ADR-0024 owns only the shape of the Filter's query surface.
- Presentation never reads another presenter's private state. A presenter may call a getter on a **strictly earlier stage's** product (the camera pose, the beam pose, the decoy list). Each presenter declares `reads: Array[int]` of stage ids at registration and the driver's freeze check fails boot if any entry is not strictly less than the presenter's own stage. A visual presenter never reads the Audio presenter or any audio level, bus meter, cue or voice state (TR-audio-042); Audio is stage 8 and nothing reads from it.
- The simulation (`src/kernel/`, `src/sim/`) never names a presentation class, a `Node`-derived class, `CanvasItem`, `Camera2D` or `Viewport`. `zoom`, `k`, `k_auto` and `field_h` appear only under `src/presentation/` and the Pipeline root (TR-shipbody-044); a lint checks the identifiers.
- Presentation reads settings (reduced motion, reduce flashing) from the settings store; **no simulation callable reads a setting**, and no toggle writes a block. A test runs one command stream with each toggle on and off and compares the tick count and `state_hash` (TR-pxl-034).
- **Cosmetic randomness: presentation hashes use `Ihash` or `Ihash.h32` (ADR-0005 § 2.6) with a fixed non-zero per-system seed**, never the global RNG, never `RandomNumberGenerator`, and **never `DetRng.derive` (ADR-0005 bans it in presentation)**. PF-37's "no dependence on integer overflow" wording is waived for the `Ihash` family because 64-bit wrap is the pinned, golden-tested behaviour (TD-29); the Perception Filter's D.14 keeps its masked hash until ADR-0024 migrates it, and D.14's specific form is ADR-0024's. A truth-channel visual that must be reproducible (a trail) **reads `Ihash` keyed by `world_seed` (ADR-0005 § 2.6)** with a fixed per-system seed, because the simulation never draws the `trail.vis` value (TD-28); it writes nothing back.

**Write allow-list (PRESENTATION and INPUT_SURFACE):** `CanvasItem` properties (including `position`, `visible`, `modulate`, `z_index`, `frame`, `flip_h`, `texture` and so on, with the placement rule of § 4), `Material` and shader parameters, `Light2D`, `LightOccluder2D` and `CanvasModulate` properties, particle properties, and audio-player and audio-bus properties through the Audio presenter. Never: a block, a command (outside § 7), a physics body, `Camera2D.*`, `Viewport.*`, `SubViewport.*`, `SubViewportContainer.*` or `CanvasLayer.*` members **outside the Pipeline root and the camera host** (PR-8 item 4 and its lint AC), `Engine.time_scale`, `SceneTree.paused` (pause is the control plane's `PauseGate`, ADR-0002), synthetic input (`Input.parse_input_event`, `Input.action_press`), and file I/O (Settings and the Save host have their own owners).

**The Layout PROJECTOR never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D`** (TR-section-024); Lighting's occluder builder is also a PROJECTOR and is the one class that does. The declared-classes list at registration is what the lint compares. The PROJECTOR scene shape, the Y-sort key and `entity_id` namespaces belong to ADR-0034 (this ADR owns placement only).

A presenter output signal that crosses into simulation does not exist: the flow is state, notification, presentation, and never the reverse (CR-10 "Sim never calls presentation").

input.content:
### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages

**`PipelineRoot` is the `PresentationHost`** (ruling TD-03; ADR-0008 owns the edit to its § 6.1, § 6.2 and § 7.3). It is one `Node` with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code, and it owns a `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree). Its single `_process(delta)` does, in this order: (1) advance `present_time` (frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED`), (2) the zoom cooldown, (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty, (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`. **No second node runs at `PRESENTATION` for presentation work**, so the priority-0 tie is removed by construction rather than by tree order, and `present_time` is current when the driver runs (this closes the host and ordering questions that earlier drafts left to ADR-0008). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.

This is the "explicit driver" the HUD GDD asks for (OQ-HS-44, OQ-HS-51, ADR candidate F). It replaces N nodes whose relative order would depend on priority sub-constants and tree order with one loop over a fixed-size array, which is testable headless with stub presenters (AC-HS-89) and does not depend on the cross-node `process_priority` result for any presenter. Only the order **host after TickDriver** depends on ADR-0001's verified order, which the windowed 4.7.2 editor run confirmed and KRN-LAT-02 confirms on a desktop release export.

**Why the solve is in the driver and not in `frame_pre_draw`.** The windowed probe shows `frame_pre_draw` firing after every node `_process`, so a camera solve placed inside it is invisible to the HUD stage and gives the HUD a one-frame lag on `world_to_hud`. The solve therefore runs in stage `CAMERA_SOLVE`, and the `frame_pre_draw` handler only writes `canvas_transform` and the parallax offsets from the solved pose. **Fallback**, used only if `frame_pre_draw` fails the release-export spike (ADR-0008 pipeline spike step 12): that write moves to the end of `PipelineRoot._process`, after `driver.frame`; no new priority constant is needed.

```gdscript
# src/presentation/pipeline/presentation_stage.gd (no new directory: the shared files live in the existing Pipeline module, ADR-0010)
# Named constants only; nobody writes a literal stage number.
class_name PresentationStage extends RefCounted
const PROJECT: int = 0         # PROJECTOR builds and rebuilds, chunked: layout projector, body.projector, then the occluder builder
const CAMERA_SOLVE: int = 1    # CameraSolver computes pose_q and world_to_hud; the canvas write is in frame_pre_draw
const AVATAR: int = 2          # Avatar Presenter: position, frame, flip, beam pose
const FILTER: int = 3          # Perception Filter step, decoy list, perceived() memo
const INSTRUMENTS: int = 4
const HUD: int = 5
const LIGHTING: int = 6        # reads the beam pose (AVATAR) and the decoy list (FILTER)
const TRAIL: int = 7           # Failure & Trail (truth channel, reads no Filter product)
const AUDIO: int = 8
const DEBUG: int = 9

# src/presentation/pipeline/presentation_discontinuity.gd
class_name PresentationDiscontinuity extends RefCounted
const RESTORE: int = 0         # restore, cold load or new game: PresentationClock.load_seq changed
const CAMERA_CUT: int = 1      # the camera stage called driver.notify_camera_cut()
```

**Stage 0 holds three registrants, and their order is declared, not incidental.** The layout projector, `body.projector` and Lighting's occluder builder all register at `PROJECT`. The occluder builder depends on the tiles the layout projector builds, so a tie would otherwise be an order that varies. `Array.sort_custom` is not stable in Godot (probed, § Engine Compatibility), so the driver does **not** sort descriptors with a comparator: `freeze()` builds one packed integer key per descriptor, `stage * 1024 + registration_index`, sorts the `Array[int]` with plain `Array.sort()` (ADR-0005 § 1.7's recommendation) and runs the descriptors in key order. Within a stage the order is therefore **registration order, fixed by the composition root**, and a descriptor that needs a same-stage predecessor names it in `after`; `freeze()` fails boot if a named predecessor is not registered earlier in the same stage. The composition root registers the layout projector, then `body.projector`, then the occluder builder.

**The pinned partial order and why this total order satisfies it.** Every source that states an edge is satisfied:
- HUD AC-HS-89 and TR-hud-022: camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting. Stages 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.
- PF-35 and TR-percfilter-025: Avatar, then Filter, then Lighting reads the decoy list. Stages 2, 3, 6.
- TR-pc-040: the Presenter's beam pose is written before Lighting applies. Stages 2, 6.
- Instruments call `perceived()`, so they follow the Filter. Stages 3, 4.
- The rest (Trail, Audio, Debug after Lighting) is a convention. It differs from the order in `architecture.md` § Data Flow (Avatar, Lighting, Trail, Instruments, HUD, Audio), which the three GDD-stated edges override; § GDD sync lists the rewrite. The technical-director ruled (TD-22) that this stage order stands because it satisfies AC-HS-89 and PF-35.
- **Camera versus Avatar.** Pipeline C2 asks for the camera "ordered after the actor" so that both compose the same interpolated position. This ADR gets the same guarantee by construction, not by order: the solver and the Avatar Presenter both call `Placement.at` with the same `PresentFrame` values, so they cannot disagree. The solver runs first because the HUD needs `world_to_hud` before it draws (TR-hud-022). Step 12 of the pipeline spike (zero render-px disagreement) tests the claim.

```gdscript
# src/presentation/pipeline/presenter_descriptor.gd
# RefCounted by rule: a descriptor that became a Node or Resource would collide `name` with Node.name / Resource.resource_name.
class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted
var name: StringName
var stage: int                        # a PresentationStage constant
var reads: Array[int]                 # stages whose products this presenter calls; each must be < stage
var after: Array[StringName]          # same-stage presenters that must be registered earlier (intra-stage order); usually empty
var present: Callable                 # (frame: PresentFrame) -> void; standard method Callable, exactly one argument
var on_discontinuity: Callable        # (kind: int) -> void; kind is a PresentationDiscontinuity constant; standard method Callable, exactly one argument

# src/presentation/pipeline/present_frame.gd
class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted     # one object, reused every frame; fields overwritten, never reallocated
var alpha: float            # clock.tick_alpha read ONCE per frame; in [0, 1]; 1.0 while not RUNNING
var T: int                  # last committed tick; may feed values the simulation also computes, never cosmetic phase
var running: bool
var present_time: float     # supplied by PipelineRoot (ADR-0008); frozen while PAUSED; the only cosmetic clock
var present_delta: float    # present_time minus the previous frame's present_time; 0.0 while PAUSED; drives manual animation advance (§ 5)
var render_delta: float     # engine _process delta, scaled by Engine.time_scale, CLAMPED by the driver to ADR-0008's DT_MAX; smoothing filters only, never a phase

# src/presentation/pipeline/presentation_driver.gd
class_name PresentationDriver extends RefCounted
func register(desc: PresenterDescriptor) -> void          # BOOTING only
func freeze() -> void                                      # builds packed stage*1024+index keys, Array.sort(); fails boot on any check below
func frame(host_delta: float, present_time: float) -> void # fills PresentFrame, handles load_seq, runs the stages
func notify_camera_cut() -> void                           # called by the camera stage; next frame every presenter gets CAMERA_CUT
```

**`freeze()` checks, all boot failures:** names are unique; every `reads` entry is strictly less than the descriptor's `stage`; every `after` name is a presenter of the same stage registered earlier; `present.is_valid()`, `present.is_standard()` and `present.get_argument_count() == 1`; and the same three for `on_discontinuity`. `present` and `on_discontinuity` are untyped `Callable`s, so without the arity check a wrong signature would fail only at call time on the first frame the presenter runs (`Callable.get_argument_count` exists in 4.7.2, probed).

`present` and `on_discontinuity` are registered `Callable`s returning `void`. They are **not** kernel-invoked owner callables, so ADR-0003's `CompletionToken` rule does not apply to them, and registering `Callable`s rather than overriding a base class avoids the 4.7 typed-return override rule altogether (ADR-0003 § 1 makes the same choice for owners). That rule would bite only if a base presenter class declared a typed non-void virtual for handlers, which this ADR forbids unless ADR-0010 introduces one with the conditions in Implementation Guidelines. A `-> void` override under an `@abstract` base needs no `return`.

**`render_delta` and `present_time`.** Both derive from the engine's `_process` delta, which is scaled by `Engine.time_scale` and arrives as one huge value after a main-loop stall (a Windows window drag or resize, focus loss, a shader-compile hitch). The driver therefore clamps `render_delta` to the same `DT_MAX` as ADR-0008's camera solver, so a smoothing filter fed it does not jump. `present_time` itself advances by whatever ADR-0008 says (this ADR does not decide whether a stall advances it); `present_delta` is whatever `present_time` advanced.

**Driver rules.** The driver iterates a fixed-size array, allocates nothing, checks `present.is_valid()` before each call and skips and counts a freed presenter (`PRESENTER_DEAD`, as ADR-0002 does for result handlers), and **never runs a presenter inside a tick**. Presenter faults cannot fault the kernel: nothing here runs in a tick phase. Stage timing exists in dev and playtest builds through ADR-0001's diagnostics timer and is compiled out of release.

**The frame object is the clock.** `PresentFrame.alpha` is read once; no presenter reads `PresentationClock.tick_alpha` directly (a lint allows the `tick_alpha` read only in `presentation_driver.gd`, ADR-0010 TD-17; tests inject a `PresentFrame`, and the camera solver's pure-function twin takes alpha as an argument). This guarantees one alpha per frame. A presenter may read `frame.T` for values the simulation also computes (the beacon aim at `T`, a Graph step index); it **must never** use `T` or any tick counter as cosmetic phase (registry `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`), and uses `frame.present_time` for cosmetic phase.

**Pause.** `PresentFrame.present_time` is frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED` and `alpha` is 1.0, so a presenter that computes from `present_time` and `alpha` is frozen without being told. Layers 3 and 4 (Chart Table) keep running on engine time because they must respond while paused (PR-9); they are INPUT_SURFACE objects and UI Controls, not world presenters.

### 3. One driver, one frame object, fixed named stages

**`PipelineRoot` is the `PresentationHost`** (ruling TD-03; ADR-0008 owns the edit to its § 6.1, § 6.2 and § 7.3). It is one `Node` with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and `process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, set from code, and it owns a `PresentationDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree). Its single `_process(delta)` does, in this order: (1) advance `present_time` (frozen while the kernel is `PAUSED`), (2) the zoom cooldown, (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty, (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`. **No second node runs at `PRESENTATION` for presentation work**, so the priority-0 tie is removed by construction rather than by tree order, and `present_time` is current when the driver runs (this closes the host and ordering questions that earlier drafts left to ADR-0008). **Presenters define no `_process`.** They register a `PresenterDescriptor` with the driver in `BOOTING`; the driver freezes the registry with the kernel and sorts it once by stage.

This is the "explicit driver" the HUD GDD asks for (OQ-HS-44, OQ-HS-51, ADR candidate F). It replaces N nodes whose relative order would depend on priority sub-constants and tree order with one loop over a fixed-size array, which is testable headless with stub presenters (AC-HS-89) and does not depend on the cross-node `process_priority` result for any presenter. Only the order **host after TickDriver** depends on ADR-0001's verified order, which the windowed 4.7.2 editor run confirmed and KRN-LAT-02 confirms on a desktop release export.

The solve therefore runs in stage `CAMERA_SOLVE`, and the `frame_pre_draw` handler only writes `canvas_transform` and the parallax offsets from the solved pose. **Fallback**, used only if `frame_pre_draw` fails the release-export spike (ADR-0008 pipeline spike step 12): that write moves to the end of `PipelineRoot._process`, after `driver.frame`; no new priority constant is needed.

const AVATAR: int = 2          # Avatar Presenter: position, frame, flip, beam pose
const FILTER: int = 3          # Perception Filter step, decoy list, perceived() memo
const INSTRUMENTS: int = 4
const HUD: int = 5
const LIGHTING: int = 6        # reads the beam pose (AVATAR) and the decoy list (FILTER)

const AUDIO: int = 8
const DEBUG: int = 9

class_name PresenterDescriptor extends RefCounted
var name: StringName
var stage: int                        # a PresentationStage constant
var reads: Array[int]                 # stages whose products this presenter calls; each must be < stage
var after: Array[StringName]          # same-stage presenters that must be registered earlier (intra-stage order); usually empty
var present: Callable                 # (frame: PresentFrame) -> void; standard method Callable, exactly one argument

# src/presentation/pipeline/present_frame.gd
class_name PresentFrame extends RefCounted     # one object, reused every frame; fields overwritten, never reallocated
var alpha: float            # clock.tick_alpha read ONCE per frame; in [0, 1]; 1.0 while not RUNNING

### 5. One interpolator: physics interpolation off, and no engine clock on sim-visible content

**The pins.** `physics/common/physics_interpolation` is **absent or `false` in `project.godot`**; the effective value is checked through `ProjectSettings.get_setting` in the post-first-frame boot check and in a gdUnit4 test (ADR-0008 § 5.5(a), effective-value tier), because a value equal to the default is not serialised and a `ConfigFile` read cannot confirm an absent key's effective value (TD-21; ADR-0010 PRJ-02 moves this key from presence checks to the effective-value tier). The presentation root nodes set `physics_interpolation_mode = Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF` (value 2; the bare word `OFF` is not valid GDScript) and children inherit. `Camera2D.position_smoothing_enabled = false` and `limit_smoothed = false` where a `Camera2D` exists at all (the primary camera variant has none in the world tree, PR-6 C2).

**The boot check, after the first `SceneTree.process_frame`** (probed: inheritance propagates lazily, so a read before the first frame can disagree with a read after it, and a node added later reads correctly immediately): `ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/common/physics_interpolation") == false`, `get_tree().physics_interpolation == false`, and a walk over every node under the presentation roots asserts `not node.is_physics_interpolated()`. Because `is_physics_interpolated()` **ignores the global enable flag** (probed), the walk asserts explicit `OFF` inheritance from an `OFF` root, not effective interpolation, and that is why the roots must be explicit `OFF`. class_name Placement extends RefCounted
## Interpolate previous to current at alpha, then floor, per axis. alpha is clamped by the caller's PresentFrame.
static func at(prev: Vector2i, curr: Vector2i, alpha: float) -> Vector2i:
	return Vector2i(floori(prev.x + (curr.x - prev.x) * alpha), floori(prev.y + (curr.y - prev.y) * alpha))

## Alpha for a block whose owner runs every n ticks and publishes the tick it last ran (Horror alpha_5, PR-9).
static func alpha_n(run_tick: int, T: int, alpha: float, n: int) -> float:
	return clampf((float(T - run_tick) + alpha) / float(n), 0.0, 1.0)

## Floor a float vector to whole pixels, per axis. The integer helper for derived offsets that are not a prev/curr pair
## (the camera host's parallax layer offsets are built from this, never from a bare floor(); ADR-0008 § 6.2).
static func floor_v(v: Vector2) -> Vector2i:
	return Vector2i(floori(v.x), floori(v.y))

static func put(node: Node2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
	var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p)

### 7. `INPUT_SURFACE` is the only submitting class, and a class is not a right

- A command can be submitted only by an object that holds a `SurfaceHandle` (ADR-0002) **and** was registered as `INPUT_SURFACE`. Subscribing as `INPUT_SURFACE` confers no submit right (registry `presentation_submit_without_handle`): the Interaction prompt object subscribes without a handle. A `PRESENTATION` facet has no submit method and no way to obtain a handle.
- **Boot check at the freeze, limited to `SurfaceHandle`s:** every name passed to `issue_surface_handle` has an `INPUT_SURFACE` registration with the same name, and no `SurfaceHandle` name matches a `PRESENTATION`, `PROJECTOR` or `DIAGNOSTIC` registration.
